title: Plugins epic: gRPC plugin protocol + openclaw compat shim
description: Talon's drop-in goal requires supporting both (a) existing openclaw Node.js plugins from dist/extensions/ and (b) new native-language plugins (Go, Rust, Python, ...). Mechanism: subprocess plugins exposing a gRPC service. Each plugin runs as its own process; talon manages lifecycle (spawn, handshake, health, restart on crash) and dials the plugin's gRPC server. Hashicorp go-plugin is the canonical library for this pattern but we can roll a thin custom version if it's overkill. Existing openclaw extensions are reached via a special 'openclaw-plugin-host' subprocess (Node.js) that loads their JS via openclaw's loader and translates their hooks to our gRPC service — drops-in for the user's current channels (telegram), tools (brave), and providers (anthropic-via-claude-cli) without requiring rewrites.

title: sessions.patch + sessions.list + sessions.subscribe; per-session model override in chat.send
description: The UI fails to change models with 'unknown method: sessions.patch'. Implement: (1) sessions.patch {key, model?, thinkingLevel?, verboseLevel?, fastMode?} stores a per-session prefs map; treats explicit null as 'clear'. (2) sessions.list returns the openclaw envelope {ts, path, count, defaults, sessions[]} including any sessions that have been patched OR have chat history. (3) sessions.subscribe is a no-op {ok:true} so the UI's subscribe call doesn't error; live presence events come later. (4) chat.send consults SessionPrefs.model BEFORE resolving the agent's PrimaryModel — UI override wins, provider derived from the override's ModelID. Other patch fields (thinkingLevel/verboseLevel/fastMode) are stored but not yet wired into chat.send.
close_reason: sessions.{patch,list,subscribe} land + per-session model override is honored by chat.send. SessionStore (sessionKey → SessionPref{Fields:map[string]json.RawMessage,UpdatedAt}) is mutex-guarded for concurrent reads from chat goroutines while the UI patches. Patch fields are stored as raw JSON so we can accept any patch shape openclaw's UI sends; explicit null clears a field. Helper SessionStore.Model(key) is called by ChatHandler.runStream BEFORE PrimaryModel resolution — UI override wins; provider derived from the override's ModelID.Provider() so model-switching across providers (openai → deepseek) Just Works. sessions.patch returns {ok,path,key,entry} mirroring openclaw's SessionsPatchResultBase. sessions.list returns {ts,path,count,defaults,sessions[]} (SessionsListResult shape) and includes both patched sessions and chat-only sessions (via ChatStore.Keys()). sessions.subscribe is a no-op {ok:true} — live presence events come later. Tests: store patch+null-clear, model helper, snapshot-is-a-copy, sessions.patch happy + missing-key, sessions.list combined source, subscribe ack, chat.send override wins, no-override uses default, compat for sessions.patch result shape.

title: agent.identity.get: accept sessionKey param (UI doesn't send agentId)
description: The openclaw web UI calls agent.identity.get with {sessionKey} (controllers/assistant-identity.ts: 'const params = sessionKey ? { sessionKey } : {}'). Our handler requires agentId and returns BAD_REQUEST. The UI's try/catch swallows the error silently, so the chat label sticks on the boot default 'Assistant' instead of resolving to 'Clawdia'. Fix: accept agentId OR sessionKey OR neither (default to 'main' — matching openclaw's resolveDefaultAgentId fallback). Derive agentId from sessionKey via the existing AgentIDFromSessionKey helper. Add a compat test that locks the request shape.
close_reason: agent.identity.get now resolves the agent in three tiers: explicit agentId → derived from sessionKey via AgentIDFromSessionKey → default 'main'. Mirrors openclaw's resolveDefaultAgentId fallback. Fixes the silent-failure bug where the UI's controllers/assistant-identity.ts call ('agent.identity.get', {sessionKey}) hit our agentId-required handler, got BAD_REQUEST, the catch swallowed it, and the chat label never updated from 'Assistant' to 'Clawdia'. Compat test added: TestCompat_AgentIdentityGetAcceptsSessionKeyParam locks the contract; sessionKey-only request must succeed and return the workspace IDENTITY.md name. Three additional unit tests cover no-params-defaults-to-main, all three sessionKey forms, and explicit agentId winning over sessionKey.

title: openai: empty content serialized as null breaks 400
description: OpenAI returned 'Invalid value for content: expected a string, got null' on a message[44] (tool result with empty output OR assistant turn with only tool_calls). buildRequestBody used omitempty on Content, dropping the field for empty strings; OpenAI maps missing content to null and rejects. Fix: drop omitempty on Content so it's always emitted as a string.
close_reason: Dropped omitempty on Content in oaiMessage so the field always serializes as a string (empty when no text). Tool result turns with no output and assistant-only-tool_calls turns now produce {role,content:'',tool_calls:[...]} or {role:'tool',tool_call_id,content:''} — both shapes OpenAI accepts. Regression test TestStream_EmptyContentIsExplicitStringNotNull asserts content:'' is present and content:null never appears.

title: E2E test suite with testcontainers (plugin focus)
description: Boot talon-gateway in a Docker container via testcontainers-go and exercise plugin lifecycle end-to-end. Validates real subprocess plugins through real gateway with the same wire-protocol the user sees. Same harness will host openclaw Node.js compat shim tests (talon-o0h) when that lands.
close_reason: Shipped: internal/e2e harness boots talon-gateway via testcontainers-go (Dockerfile.test bakes talon + testplugin into alpine), runs config-driven scenarios, captures container logs into in-memory buffer for assertions. Two tests so far: TestE2E_PluginChannelRoundtrip exercises full StartChannel→ChatHandler.RunForSession→testprov stream→SendChannelMessage flow using testchan + testprov/echo-1; TestE2E_PluginLoadsAndAnnounces verifies spawn/handshake/manifest. Behind //go:build e2e tag; runs via 'make test-e2e'. Harness API extends naturally to Node.js compat shim (talon-o0h) — Dockerfile.test will grow a Node layer and tests just specify a different plugins.entries.<name>.cmd path.

title: Host service implementation: capability-gated plugin → host RPCs
description: Implement pb.HostServer methods (GetConfig, ListAgents, GetAgentIdentity, ListModels, ListSessions, GetChatHistory, AppendMemory, RunSubagent) by adapting talon's existing handlers (ReadHandler, ChatHandler, SessionsHandler, memory.Append). Spin up a separate gRPC listener at gateway startup, register HostService with the Host's UnaryInterceptor + StreamInterceptor for capability gating, advertise the listen address to plugins via plugin.NewHost(addr) so loaded plugins can dial back. server.Server gains ChatHandler/ChatStore/SessionStore accessors so cmd/talon can wire HostService against the same shared state the WS surface uses. Out of scope: streaming-completion forwarding (StreamCompletion is on Plugin service, host calls plugin not vice versa); channel send (still in talon-13z).
close_reason: Host service implementation lands. internal/server/hostsvc.go: HostService implements pb.HostServer for GetConfig/ListAgents/GetAgentIdentity/ListModels/ListSessions/GetChatHistory/AppendMemory/RunSubagent. Each method delegates to the existing in-process handler logic (ReadHandler.handleConfigGet, handleAgentsList, handleAgentIdentityGet, handleModelsList; SessionsHandler.handleList; ChatHandler.handleHistory + RunInline; memory.Append) so plugins see the same shape and same data the WS surface does — no drift between UI and plugin views. JSON-shaped responses ride raw_json fields. GetConfig respects the optional path scope via gjson; secrets are redacted exactly the same as the WS path. AppendMemory resolves agentId → workspace via the same three-tier precedence as the WS memory.append. server.Server gained ChatHandler/ChatStore/SessionStore/ReadHandler accessors (chat may be nil; reads always non-nil with paths fallback). cmd/talon/gateway.go: net.Listen ephemeral 127.0.0.1:0 → plugin.NewHost(addr) → server.New (so handlers exist) → NewHostService wiring → grpc.NewServer with Host UnaryInterceptor + StreamInterceptor → goroutine Serve → loadConfiguredPlugins (so plugins dial back into a live host service) → defer pluginHost.Shutdown + grpcSrv.GracefulStop. Startup log includes 'host-svc=<addr>' so users can see the back-channel is live. 12 HostService tests cover all 8 methods + edge cases (full + scoped GetConfig, secret redaction, missing path → null, identity from IDENTITY.md, chat-not-configured Unimplemented, missing-workspace error, sessions union).

title: Wire plugin Host into talon-gateway lifecycle + config-driven plugin loader
description: Plumb the plugin host into the running gateway: cmd/talon constructs a *plugin.Host at startup, walks plugins.entries.<name>.cmd in the merged config, calls LoadPlugin for each. server.Config.ToolRunnerFor closure wraps tools.NewWithSubagent in a plugin.NewToolRouter so loaded plugins' tools show up in chat. Gateway shutdown calls host.Shutdown() so subprocesses get a clean exit. Startup log lists the loaded plugin names. Host gRPC service (where plugins call back) is NOT served yet — empty hostAddr; back-channel calls fail until that lands separately. Tools-only plugins work end-to-end without back-channel access.
close_reason: Plugin host wired into gateway lifecycle. cmd/talon constructs *plugin.Host with empty hostAddr (back-channel not served yet), calls loadConfiguredPlugins which walks plugins.entries.<name>, parses {enabled, cmd:[...]} via parsePluginSpecs, then host.LoadPlugin per entry. Failures log but don't abort startup. ToolRunnerFor closure built by newToolRunnerFactory(host) wraps tools.NewWithSubagent in plugin.NewToolRouter so loaded plugins' tools surface live in chat (via ToolRouter's per-call host.List() walk). Gateway shutdown defers host.Shutdown() so subprocesses get clean exit. Startup log includes 'plugins=N' count. parsePluginSpecs is a pure function for testability — 4 tests cover enabled+cmd filter, no-entries section, empty entries, blank-cmd-string filter. newToolRunnerFactory tested for both nil-host (delegates to base, no plugin tools) and non-nil-host (returns *plugin.ToolRouter). Smoke-tested gateway startup: log line includes 'subagent' tool + plugins=0 count, defer chain triggers on shutdown.

title: Plugins: openclaw Node.js compat shim
description: One specific plugin subprocess (openclaw-plugin-host) — a Node.js process that loads an openclaw extension via openclaw's own loader and translates its hooks to our gRPC plugin service. Shipping this means existing openclaw plugins (telegram, brave, anthropic-via-claude-cli) Just Work without rewriting. Slow path (Node startup, IPC per call) but correct. Plugin is configured by pointing plugins.entries.<name>.cmd at openclaw-plugin-host with the extension path as argv. Depends on gRPC service + host runtime.
close_reason: Phase 1 shipped: apps/openclaw-plugin-host (Node.js, ESM) loads an openclaw extension, captures register*() calls (registerTool fully bridged, others captured-but-warned), starts a gRPC Plugin server, and answers Initialize with a manifest built from registered tools. Same handshake env as Go plugins. Dockerfile.test includes a Node layer + the shim + a fixture; e2e test TestE2E_OpenclawShim_LoadsExtension verifies the spawn/handshake/manifest path. Phase 2 (tracked separately): full RunTool dispatch end-to-end via WS chat, plus richer ctx (config, runtime services); registerHttpRoute / registerProvider / registerWebSearchProvider / registerChannel bridges; auto-download Node runtime if missing.

title: Plugins: channel plugin support (in/out)
description: Bidirectional message channels (Telegram, Slack, Discord, etc.). Plugin opens a server-streaming OnIncomingChannelMessage method that talon listens to and dispatches inbound messages into chat.send. Outbound (assistant text → channel delivery) routed via SendChannelMessage. Routing rules: which agent gets which inbound message (matches on user/group identifiers). Depends on the runtime + integration into the chat handler so assistant text gets fanned out.
close_reason: ChannelDispatcher pumps StartChannel inbound stream → ChatHandler.RunForSession with deterministic per-(channel,sender|room) sessionKey → SendChannelMessage outbound. Wired into gateway.go via startConfiguredChannels. RunForSession refactor extracted from RunInline. testplugin extended with testchan; full e2e test in spawn_test.go. Unit tests cover binding parsing, dispatcher lifecycle (Start/Wait/Stop, idempotency, error tolerance), session-key derivation.

title: Plugins: provider plugin support
description: Migrate provider.Provider to be served via gRPC StreamCompletion. Plugins implement provider streaming the same way internal/provider/openai does today, but via gRPC. The agentProviderFactory's switch becomes a lookup against loaded plugins keyed by provider name. internal/provider/openai and /deepseek either become embedded (in-process) plugins or their own subprocess plugins; tradeoff is startup cost vs. uniformity. Depends on gRPC service + host runtime.
close_reason: Provider plugin support landed end-to-end. internal/plugin/provider.go: PluginProvider adapts pb.PluginClient to provider.Provider so the chat handler's existing StreamCompletion routing flow doesn't change. Stream translates provider.Request → pb.StreamCompletionRequest (model with provider prefix stripped, system passthrough, messages with role/tool_calls/tool_call_id, tools with raw JSON schema bytes, optional temperature/max-tokens), opens server-stream, pumps each pb.Delta back as provider.Delta via translateDelta. Mid-stream errors emit DeltaError before close (matching openai/deepseek paths). EOF closes cleanly. Wrong provider segment in ModelID rejected before the dial. internal/plugin/host.go gained ProviderByName + ChannelByName lookups for resolving manifest.OffersProviders / OffersChannels by name. cmd/talon/gateway_chat.go: agentProviderFactory grows a *plugin.Host field; resolution order is openai → deepseek → loaded-plugin-by-name → ErrProviderUnavailable. testplugin extended with offers_providers=[testprov→echo-1] and a StreamCompletion impl that echoes the user's last message. Tests: 12 unit tests (all 5 Delta variants translated, nil/empty translateDelta returns false, content/tool-call/error field roundtrips, PluginProvider Stream happy path with request translation verified, wrong-provider rejection, setup-error propagation, mid-flight error → DeltaError + close, ProviderByName + ChannelByName lookups). 1 integration test spawns testplugin and exercises the full PluginProvider.Stream end-to-end against a real subprocess.

title: Plugins: subprocess host runtime in talon
description: Lifecycle manager for plugin subprocesses. Per plugin: spawn (with handshake env vars for port + auth cookie), wait for ready, dial gRPC, health-check, restart on unexpected exit, clean shutdown. Modeled on Hashicorp go-plugin's transport but our own thin wrapper since we don't need their full feature surface. Plugins discovered via plugins.entries.<name>.cmd in config (path to plugin binary) — opt-in, opt-out via the existing enabled flag. Depends on the gRPC service definition.
close_reason: Subprocess plugin host runtime landed in internal/plugin. Handshake protocol (handshake.go): host sets TALON_PLUGIN_HANDSHAKE/AUTH_COOKIE/HOST_ADDR env, plugin prints '1|TCP|<addr>|grpc' as first stdout line, host parses, dials, calls Plugin.Initialize. Subsequent stdout lines forwarded as '[plugin/<name>] <line>' for debug visibility. Auth cookie is 24-byte (192-bit) random hex; plugin echoes it back via 'talon-plugin-auth-cookie' gRPC metadata header on every Host-service call. Host (host.go): mutex-guarded registry indexed by name AND cookie (so callers and capability checks share one map). Register/Unregister/Get/List/Shutdown. Capability interceptor (host.go): closed map of method full-name → required Capability; missing mapping returns Internal (closed-set rule), missing cookie/unknown cookie returns Unauthenticated, capability mismatch returns PermissionDenied with the missing-capability name. Wraps both unary and stream paths. Stamps resolved plugin name onto ctx via CallerNameFromContext for downstream handlers. LoadPlugin (spawn.go): exec.Command + handshake-line read with timeout + grpc.NewClient + WaitForStateChange to surface dial failures fast + stop closure that tries graceful Shutdown RPC, closes conn, kills process. Lifecycle goroutine watches Wait() and unregisters on subprocess exit. testplugin/main.go: minimal stub plugin that exits if handshake env missing, opens a free TCP port, prints handshake, serves Plugin.Initialize returning a fixed 2-capability manifest. Tests: 12 unit tests (registry, duplicate-name, no-manifest, init error, unregister-stop, capability grant/deny, missing/unknown cookie, unmapped method, handshake parse valid/invalid) + 3 integration tests (end-to-end subprocess load via go-build, missing Cmd, nonexistent binary). go.mod gained google.golang.org/grpc + google.golang.org/protobuf.

title: Plugins: tool plugin support (registry integration)
description: First user-visible plugin surface: tools registered by plugins show up in chat alongside builtins. Wire ListTools/RunTool from the gRPC service into the tool registry (when running a chat.send, query each loaded plugin for its tools and union with the built-in registry). Plugin tool calls dispatch through gRPC RunTool. Validates the protocol on the smallest useful surface. Depends on gRPC service + host runtime.
close_reason: Tool plugin support landed. internal/plugin/tools.go: ToolRouter unions a LocalRunner (the existing tools.Registry / NewWithSubagent) with the *Host's currently-registered plugins. Specs() returns base + each plugin's manifest.OffersTools converted from pb.ToolSpec → provider.ToolSpec. Run() dispatches local-first (so builtin/subagent collisions favor the host); on tools.ErrUnknownTool from base, walks plugins by manifest.OffersTools name, dispatches via Plugin.RunTool gRPC. is_error=true responses surface as Go errors with the plugin output preserved; transport errors are wrapped with the plugin name. Context propagation: WithAgentID/AgentIDFromContext + WithRunID/RunIDFromContext stamp agent + run on ctx so plugins can scope per-agent and correlate logs; chat.go's runChatLoop stamps both before tool dispatch. testplugin extended to offer 'test-echo' tool whose RunTool echoes args + agent + run. Tests: 9 unit tests (Specs union, base-only when host nil, local-prefers-on-collision, plugin dispatch on unknown local, ErrUnknownTool propagation, is_error surfacing, transport error wrapping, context roundtrips for agent/run) + 1 integration test (real subprocess + ToolRouter dispatching test-echo end-to-end with verified agent/run propagation).

title: Plugins: gRPC service definition + generated stubs
description: The wire contract every plugin (native or compat-shim) implements. Methods to define: Initialize(handshake), Shutdown, ListTools, RunTool, ListProviders, StreamCompletion, ListChannels, OnIncomingChannelMessage (server-streaming from plugin), SendChannelMessage, ListSubagents (later). Messages mirror our existing internal types (ToolSpec, ToolCall, Delta, Message) but as protobuf. Land internal/plugin/proto/*.proto + generated Go stubs. Out of scope: actual host runtime (separate issue) and openclaw shim.
close_reason:
gRPC plugin protocol landed at internal/plugin/proto/plugin.proto with generated stubs at internal/plugin/pb/. Two services: Plugin (host calls plugin: Initialize/Shutdown, RunTool, StreamCompletion, StartChannel/SendChannelMessage) and Host (plugin calls host: GetConfig, ListAgents, GetAgentIdentity, ListModels, ListSessions, GetChatHistory, AppendMemory, RunSubagent). Capability enum is closed (CAPABILITY_READ_*, _APPEND_MEMORY, _PATCH_SESSION, _RUN_SUBAGENT, _SEND_CHANNEL_MESSAGE) — host gates each Host-service method against plugin's effective capability set (manifest.needs ∪ user.grants − user.denies). Manifest message carries offers (tools/providers/channels) and needs (capabilities) — Plugin.Initialize returns it; host stores and enforces. Delta uses oneof for text/reasoning/usage/tool_call/error variants matching provider.Delta. Message and ToolCall mirror provider types. Sanity tests verify Manifest roundtrip, Delta oneof variants, tool-turn message roundtrip, Capability enum names stable. Makefile gained protoc --go_out=internal/plugin/pb --go_opt=paths=source_relative \
	       --go-grpc_out=internal/plugin/pb --go-grpc_opt=paths=source_relative \
	       -Iinternal/plugin/proto \
	       internal/plugin/proto/plugin.proto (regenerate from .proto) and go install google.golang.org/protobuf/cmd/protoc-gen-go@latest
go install google.golang.org/grpc/cmd/protoc-gen-go-grpc@latest (install protoc-gen-go). Out of scope and tracked as talon-bql: subprocess handshake, gRPC interceptor enforcing capability gates, plugin-runtime lifecycle.

title: Native config.get RPC on talon-gateway
description: The openclaw web UI's config screens call config.get to populate forms (auth, channels, models, plugins, etc.). Without it, those views error out. Implementation: read talon's merged config bytes (already have config.MergedBytes), accept optional {path?} param to scope the response (gjson-style or dot path), and return the JSON value at that path (or full config when path is empty). Mirrors openclaw's plugin-bootstrap config.get shape. Out of scope: config.set / mutating writes — those land later if the UI starts driving config edits.
close_reason: config.get returns the openclaw ConfigSnapshot envelope the UI's controllers/config.ts consumes: {path, exists, raw, hash, parsed, valid, config, issues}. Sources from talon's merged config (config.MergedBytes). raw is pretty-printed JSON of the redacted view; hash is sha256 of raw (UI uses for optimistic-concurrency on writes when config.set lands). Conservative redaction walks the parsed map and replaces string-valued leaves whose key is in the secret-name set: token, botToken, password, apiKey, secret, secretKey, clientSecret, refreshToken, accessToken — covers the common openclaw secrets (gateway.auth.{token,password}, channels.<x>.{token,botToken}, plugins.entries.<x>.config..apiKey, skills.entries.<x>.apiKey). Tests cover envelope shape, hash uniqueness across content changes, redaction of all six common secret paths, non-secret field preservation, and exists reflecting the talon overlay. Compat test (TestCompat_ConfigGetEnvelope) locks the shape against UI drift and verifies redaction.

title: Subagents: parallel agent invocation primitive
description: Allow the active agent to delegate work to a subagent in parallel. openclaw's setup has multiple configured agents (main, coding, research, deepwork) — each with its own model/workspace. We need: (1) 'subagent' tool that takes {agentId, prompt} and runs that agent's chat.send loop, returns the final text. (2) Parallel scheduling: when the model calls subagent multiple times in one turn, run them concurrently with bounded parallelism. (3) Result aggregation as tool results so the parent's multi-turn loop continues. ADK is a candidate runtime — its multi-agent orchestration covers (1)+(2) out of the box but adds a heavy abstraction layer. Native implementation reuses our existing chat.send + ChatStore + tool registry. Decision: native first to preserve speed; ADK reconsidered if we hit a missing primitive (planner, hierarchical agents, etc).
close_reason: Subagent tool + parallel multi-tool execution. Refactored chat.runStream into a thin goroutine wrapper around runChatLoop(ctx, sess, ...) which now returns (finalText, error). Adds ChatHandler.RunInline(ctx, agentID, message) that runs the full multi-turn loop with sess=nil under a fresh sessionKey 'subagent:<agentID>:<runId>'; events fire to no-one and the accumulated text is returned to the caller. Subagent tool in internal/tools delegates to a SubagentRunner interface (ChatHandler satisfies it). tools.NewWithSubagent(workspace, runner) registers the subagent tool alongside the builtins. Recursion is bounded by maxSubagentDepth=3 via a context-value depth counter; subagent tool refuses to fire when the limit is hit. server.Config.ToolRunnerFor signature gained a SubagentRunner argument; cmd/talon's makeToolRunner passes it through to tools.NewWithSubagent. Parallel tool execution: when the model emits multiple tool calls in one turn, runToolsParallel dispatches them concurrently with maxToolConcurrency=4; results are appended to ChatStore in original call order so the next turn's history is deterministic. Single-call path stays sequential to avoid goroutine overhead. Tests: tools subagent (delegate, missing args, depth limit, nil-runner skips, registered alongside builtins); RunInline (happy path with subagent session in store, empty-args rejection, provider error propagation); 3-tool parallel run completes in ~50ms not 150ms with maxActive≥2.

title: Memory: 'remember' tool + memory.append RPC
description: Give the model a way to record durable notes during chat. Two surfaces, both writing to the same place: (1) New 'remember' builtin tool ({text, scope?}) that the model calls when SOUL/AGENTS guidance says to. Appends to <workspace>/memory/<YYYY-MM-DD>.md (creates with H1 header on first write of the day). (2) memory.append RPC {agentId|sessionKey, text} for non-chat clients. Both share the same writer. Emits an agent.tool stream event (phase=start with text, phase=result acknowledging the write) so the UI shows the write in the tool stream. No structured store, no recall — those land later. Depends on the workspace/memory loader (talon-?) so writes are immediately visible on the next chat.send.
close_reason: Two writers, one on-disk shape: (1) 'remember' tool ({text}) registered alongside the other builtins in tools.New, calls memory.Append(workspace, text). (2) memory.append RPC ({agentId|sessionKey, text}) on talon-gateway via ReadHandler — same agent resolution as agent.identity.get (agentId → sessionKey-derived → 'main'). Both share internal/memory.Append which writes to <workspace>/memory/<YYYY-MM-DD>.md, creating the file with an H1 date header on first write of the day and appending after a blank line on subsequent writes. nowFunc is overridable for tests. Tests: 7 in internal/memory (creation, same-day append order, day rollover, empty text/workspace rejection, mkdir-on-demand, whitespace trim); 2 in internal/tools (remember tool happy path, empty rejection); 4 in internal/server (RPC writes, sessionKey path, empty text → BAD_REQUEST, missing workspace → INTERNAL). Tool-stream events for in-chat 'remember' invocations come for free via the existing chat.send → emitAgentToolStart/Result path.

title: Memory: load workspace/memory/*.md into the system prompt
description: openclaw stores per-agent durable memory as date-stamped markdown files in <workspace>/memory/ (e.g. 2026-04-26.md). agentcontext.Build currently loads MEMORY.md only. Extend it to also walk <workspace>/memory/, sort filenames descending (newest first), and inject the most recent N entries below the canonical context files. Budget by character cap (default ~16 kB total) so old journals don't blow the context window. Order in the prompt: AGENTS/SOUL/IDENTITY/USER/TOOLS/MEMORY (existing) then a new '## Recent memory' section with date-headed sub-blocks. Out of scope: structured store, vector recall, mem0/Letta — flagged for later as the md-parsing perf issue gets revisited.
close_reason: agentcontext.Build now also walks <workspace>/memory/*.md, sorts descending (newest first; YYYY-MM-DD naming gives lexical=chronological reverse), and renders a '## Recent memory' section after the canonical context files. Capped at MemoryBudgetBytes (16 KB) total; the trailing entry is truncated at the last newline before the cut and appends '[truncated to fit memory budget]'. Skips non-markdown files, blank-only entries, and missing memory/ dirs gracefully. Memory section emits even when no canonical context files are loaded (skips the load notice in that case). 6 new tests cover order, budget, memory-alone, non-md skip, blank skip, missing dir.

title: Openclaw compat regression test suite
description: Lock in the wire-protocol invariants the openclaw web UI depends on so changes that drift away from compat fail loudly. Targets: (1) handshake — connect.challenge nonce/ts shape and HelloOK envelope (protocol, server.version, features, snapshot, policy); (2) RPC envelopes — agents.list ({agents,defaultId,mainKey,scope}), models.list ({models}), config.schema (passthrough), agent.identity.get ({agentId,name,emoji,avatar}), skills.status ({workspaceDir,managedSkillsDir,skills}), chat.history (per-role row shapes: user/assistant-with-tool_use/toolResult); (3) event shapes — chat event (state in {delta,final,aborted,error}, runId echoes idempotencyKey, message.content[0].text), agent stream='tool' event (data.{toolCallId,name,phase:start|result,args|result}); (4) chat.send {sessionKey,message,idempotencyKey} request shape and {runId} response. Use gjson assertions on marshaled JSON so the tests are stable against ordering / field-presence changes that don't break the UI; reserve byte-exact only where it matters (e.g. state name strings).
close_reason: 23 compat tests in internal/server/openclaw_compat_test.go cover the wire-protocol invariants the openclaw web UI matches on. Sections: (1) Handshake — connect.challenge nonce/ts, HelloOK envelope (type='hello-ok', protocol, server.{version,connId}, features.{methods,events} as arrays, snapshot.{health,stateVersion,uptimeMs}, policy.{maxPayload,maxBufferedBytes,tickIntervalMs}, auth.role); (2) RPC envelopes — agents.list ({agents,defaultId,mainKey,scope='per-sender'}), agents.list rows ({id,model.{primary,fallbacks}}), models.list rows (id/provider/name/contextWindow:number/input:array/reasoning:bool), agent.identity.get ({agentId,name,emoji,avatar}), skills.status ({workspaceDir,managedSkillsDir,skills:array}); (3) chat.send response ({runId} echoes idempotencyKey — load-bearing for typing-indicator clearing); (4) chat events — state values 'delta'/'final'/'error' as exact strings, message.{phase:'assistant',role:'assistant',content[].type='text'}; (5) agent tool stream events — stream='tool', data.phase 'start'/'result', data.{toolCallId,name,args/result}; (6) chat.history rows per role — user (text block), assistant-with-tool_calls (text + tool_use blocks with id/name/input), toolResult (role='toolResult' EXACTLY, toolCallId, toolName, isError, content[]); (7) frame envelope — FrameReq='req', FrameRes='res', FrameEvent='event', ProtocolVersion=3, error codes (BAD_REQUEST/UNAUTHORIZED/PROTOCOL_MISMATCH/METHOD_NOT_FOUND/INTERNAL/HANDSHAKE_REQUIRED); (8) sessionKey parsing across all three openclaw-canonical forms. Uses gjson assertions so cosmetic field reordering doesn't break the suite — semantic drift does.

title: Gateway dedups sessions by clientId+instanceId on connect
description: A single UI page-load opens two simultaneous WS connections to talon-gateway (visible as two adjacent 'ws connected conn=...' log lines on the same remote IP, different ports). Likely UI-side: Lit connectedCallback firing twice on HMR or connectGateway racing with the deferred bootstrap finally. The gateway should defend against this regardless: when a new connect handshake completes with the same client.id + client.instanceId as an active session, close the older session with a structured reason (e.g. 'replaced-by-newer-instance'). Implementation: server tracks active sessions in a sync.Map keyed by 'clientId|instanceId'. After hello-ok, register; on session exit, deregister; if a key already exists, signal the old session to shut down via a context-cancel channel.
close_reason: Gateway dedups WS sessions by clientId+instanceId at end of handshake. Server tracks active sessions in a sync.Mutex-guarded map keyed by '<clientId>|<instanceId>'. Session.register inserts after hello-ok; if the key was occupied the old session.shutdown is called (StatusNormalClosure with reason 'replaced-by-newer-instance') so the displaced WS gets a clean close-frame the UI can interpret. Session.deregister uses compare-and-delete so the displaced session's defer doesn't accidentally remove its successor on the way out. Empty clientId or instanceId skips registration (CLI/no-instance clients still work, just without dedup). Tests cover: same-key replacement evicts old, different-instanceIds coexist (multi-tab), CAS prevents stale deregister, empty key is a no-op, 100-goroutine concurrent register/unregister doesn't deadlock.

title: Compose agent context files into chat.send system prompt
description:

Each non-empty file is rendered as '## <NAME>

<content>

'. SOUL.md gets a one-line preamble nudging the model to embody its persona. Implementation: new internal/agentcontext package with Build(workspace) string. Wire into chat.go's runStream once per chat.send (top of the multi-turn loop) so each call picks up edits to the files. HEARTBEAT.md / BOOTSTRAP.md / PROJECTS.md handling is out of scope for MVP.

title: chat.history emits openclaw-shaped tool_use + tool_result blocks
description: On chat reload (or scrollback) the UI renders each tool result as a generic 'Tool output' card with sublabel 'tool' instead of the invoked tool name (glob/bash/etc). Live tool stream cards work because they receive rich agent.tool events; chat.history flattens everything to {role,content:[{type:text,text}]}. openclaw's shape for tool turns is different: tool result rows are role='toolResult' with toolCallId + toolName fields and content=[{type:'text',text}], and assistant turns with tool calls carry tool_use content blocks. title: Dockerize talon-gateway for tool-testing isolation
description: The bash/write/edit tools execute in the gateway's process. Running talon-gateway in a container isolates the host while still preserving the openclaw config/auth/workspace paths the model expects. Scope: (1) multi-stage Dockerfile (golang builder → alpine runtime with /bin/sh + coreutils for tool execution, talon binary at /usr/local/bin/talon, EXPOSE 18789, ENTRYPOINT runs 'talon gateway run --bind=lan --port=18789'); (2) docker-build + docker-run + docker-stop Make targets; (3) port mapping host:18789→container:18789 (the original openclaw port — assumes the user stops openclaw first); (4) bind-mount ~/.openclaw and ~/.talon at the SAME absolute paths inside the container with HOME= so agents.list[].workspace strings (which embed host paths) resolve transparently; (5) a .dockerignore so the build context stays slim.

title: Tools: chat event payload supports tool_use + tool_result content blocks
description: The openclaw web UI's app-tool-stream renders tool calls and results from chat event content blocks: {type:'tool_use', id, name, input} and {type:'tool_result', tool_use_id, content:[{type:'text',text:...}]}. chat events emitted by talon-gateway need to include those blocks so the UI tool stream shows live progress. Per tool call: emit a chat event with state=delta and a content block with type=tool_use as soon as we begin executing; emit a follow-up with type=tool_result once the tool returns. Final assistant message in chat.history should also carry the assembled blocks so refreshes restore the visual.

Per tool call: emitAgentToolStart fires {data:{toolCallId,name,phase:'start',args:<parsed JSON or raw>}} before runner.Run, emitAgentToolResult fires {data:{toolCallId,name,phase:'result',result:<output>}} after. RunID matches the chat runId (since talon uses the client's idempotencyKey as the runId, the UI can correlate tool events back to the active chat run unlike openclaw's runtime which uses a different engine-side runId). Build helpers are pure functions tested independently: parsed-JSON args, fallback-to-raw-string on malformed JSON, result passthrough. Out of scope (talon-iod): approval prompts and exec policy.

title: Tools: multi-turn loop in chat.send
description: chat.send currently does a single provider stream then emits state=final. With tools enabled, the loop becomes: stream → on each DeltaToolCall, run the tool via the registry → append tool_result message → re-call provider with the updated history → repeat until the stream terminates with no tool_calls. Cap at MaxToolIterations (default 16) to avoid runaway loops; if the cap is hit emit state=error with errorKind='tool-loop-limit'. ChatStore message shape grows to support tool_use and tool_result content blocks (still text for plain user/assistant turns). Tests with stub provider that emits a tool_call on first stream and text on second confirm the multi-turn cycle, the iteration cap, and the proper history shape feeding back into the second call.
close_reason: Multi-turn loop landed in chat.send. Per chat.send: build tool runner once (workspace via WorkspaceResolver, registry via ToolRunnerFor factory) → iterate up to MaxToolIterations (default 16): build messages from store, attach Registry.Specs() as Request.Tools, stream → on DeltaText accumulate + emit cumulative state=delta, on DeltaToolCall buffer; when stream ends with toolCalls → AppendAssistantWithCalls + run each tool sequentially (errors captured into result string) + AppendToolResult, loop back; with no toolCalls → Append assistant text + emit state=final and return. Cap exhaustion emits state=error with errorKind='tool-loop-limit'. Model invoking tools without a configured runner emits state=error with errorKind='tool-runner-unavailable' (rather than ignoring the call and looping forever). Text-only chat without WithTools regresses to the previous single-turn behavior. ChatStore extended: AppendAssistantWithCalls (assistant turn with tool_calls), AppendToolResult (role=tool with ToolCallID). messagesFromHistory translates store rows to provider.Messages preserving tool_calls and ToolCallID. Server config grew WorkspaceResolver + ToolRunnerFor; cmd/talon wires both via configAgentResolver (also implements WorkspaceResolver now) and tools.New(workspace). Tests with scriptedProvider + stubToolRunner cover: full call → execute → re-stream cycle with correct history shape, iteration cap stops at MaxToolIterations, tool-runner-unavailable errors out cleanly, text-only mode regression.

title: Tools: builtin tool registry + read/write/bash/grep/glob impls
description: internal/tools package: Tool interface (Name, Description, ParametersSchema, Run(ctx, input json.RawMessage) (output, error)). Builtins, all workspace-scoped (paths resolved relative to a Workspace string passed at registry construction; absolute paths are rejected unless they resolve under workspace): read (file contents, line range), write (create/overwrite), edit (find/replace by string match), bash (exec a command via /bin/sh -c with timeout, capture stdout+stderr), glob (workspace-relative pattern), grep (regex over files). Each tool has a JSON schema for parameters. Registry exposes ListSpecs() []provider.ToolSpec and Run(ctx, name, input) (output, error). Tests against a temp workspace cover the workspace-confinement guard.

Six builtin tools, all workspace-confined: read (with optional line range), write (creates parent dirs), edit (errors on ambiguous or missing match — echoes Claude Code's edit semantics), bash (CombinedOutput, default 30s/max 5min timeout, exit code in trailer, cwd=workspace), glob (filepath.Glob, workspace-relative results), grep (regex via WalkDir, max 200 matches, skips .git/node_modules/.talon, supports include glob filter). resolveInWorkspace uses filepath.Rel to reject path traversal and lookalike-prefix attacks (workspace=/foo, target=/foobar/x is rejected). 23 tests cover the registry surface, every tool's happy path, traversal rejection, ambiguous-match error, exit code formatting, and context cancellation tolerance.

title: Native agent.identity.get on talon-gateway
description: The web UI calls agent.identity.get {agentId} to render the assistant's name + avatar in the chat header. title: Native chat.send + chat event stream (uses provider interface)
description: Implement chat.send and the chat event stream on talon-gateway. chat.send accepts {sessionKey, message, idempotencyKey} (matching openclaw shape) and: (1) resolves sessionKey to an agentId (default sessionKey form is agent:<agentId>:<agentId>), (2) loads that agent's primary model from merged config, (3) creates a Provider for the model's provider name (factory lookup), (4) launches a streaming completion in a goroutine, (5) fans Provider Deltas out to the originating session as 'chat' events with the openclaw event shape: {runId, sessionKey, seq, state:'streaming'|'final'|'aborted'|'error', message:{phase:'assistant',role:'assistant',content:[{type:'text',text:...}]}, errorKind?, errorMessage?}. Idempotency: if a runId is already active for {sessionKey, idempotencyKey} return the existing runId and replay events from a per-session ring buffer (cap 100 events) for late subscribers. title: OpenAI provider implementation (streaming chat completions)

title: Provider interface (internal/provider package)
description: Design and ship the streaming-completion provider interface that talon-gateway's chat.send will use. Types only in this issue — no concrete provider impl. title: Gateway WS connect handshake (login)
description: Implement the openclaw-compatible WS connect handshake on claw-gateway so the control UI can log in. Auth modes: none/token (skip password/trusted-proxy for now). Reject pre-connect frames except 'connect'. After connect, dispatch req frames to a registry; unknown methods return ErrorCodes shape.

title: Config-change policy: never auto-restart, never auto-load; HUP-reload where possible
description:
Policy decision (2026-04-27): config writes by talon must never trigger a gateway restart or auto-reload. The user explicitly opted out of file-watcher-based reloads. Where supported, a config field should be hot-reloadable via SIGHUP to the running gateway. Where not, talon's 'config set' output should tell the user a restart is needed.

Scope:
1. Path-class registry — for each known config dot-path, classify as (a) hot-reloadable on SIGHUP, (b) effective-on-next-RPC (no signal needed), (c) requires restart. Initial pass: gateway.* probably (c); channels.* probably (a); models.* probably (b); auth.profiles probably (b); plugins.entries.<x>.enabled requires restart; agents.list probably (a) for non-workspace fields.
2. cmd/talon/config set output — replace the bare 'set <path>' message with a class-aware hint:
   - (a): 'set <path>. Send SIGHUP to the running gateway to apply (or restart).'
   - (b): 'set <path>. Will be picked up on the next RPC.'
   - (c): 'set <path>. Restart the gateway to apply.'
3. Confirm openclaw's gateway actually handles SIGHUP. Today openclaw probably just re-reads on next request; SIGHUP plumbing may not exist. If so, this issue depends on adding SIGHUP support to talon's embedded gateway and/or filing an openclaw upstream issue for the same.
4. The opposite policy — talon must NEVER spawn a file watcher on ~/.openclaw or ~/.talon to auto-detect config changes. Reload is always explicit (signal or restart).
5. Document in CLAUDE.md / docs/architecture.md.

Note: openclaw's existing 'config set' output ends with 'Restart the gateway to apply' regardless of path. We are intentionally diverging from that — talon classifies per-path. PARITY.md should call this out as an intentional difference, not a parity gap.
close_reason: Phase 1 landed: internal/config/reload.go with ReloadClass enum (next-rpc/hup/restart), ClassifyReload registry, ParseReloadClass and Hint. cmd/talon config set emits class-aware hints after writes; --reload override accepts next-rpc|hup|restart for unknown paths. Restart-class entries: gateway.port/bind/auth.*, gateway.tailscale.*, gateway.controlUi.*, plugins.entries.*.enabled, plugins.deny, plugins.load.paths, skills.*. HUP class empty pending talon-gateway SIGHUP handler (Phase 2: talon-f06). Tests cover all listed paths + override parsing + Hint shapes. PARITY.md documents the intentional divergence from openclaw's 'restart to apply' universal message. CLAUDE.md updated with explicit-reload policy + registry pointers.

title: Upstream: openclaw config.schema RPC emits dangling $defs refs
description:
The schema returned by the openclaw config.schema RPC contains $ref pointers to #/$defs/<name> (secretInput, secretRef, account, audioFormatPolicy, route, stt, ...) but does not include a top-level $defs block. Instead, those definitions appear inline inside specific properties (e.g. plugins.entries.feishu.config.secretInput).

Effect on talon: schema compilation via santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6 fails with 'json-pointer in ... #/$defs/X not found'. talon's 'config validate' falls back to syntax-only and warns; 'config validate --strict' surfaces the compile error. See ErrSchemaCompileFailed in internal/config/schema.go.

Fix should land upstream in openclaw (the schema generator should either emit a top-level $defs block or rewrite the refs to point at the inline locations). Once fixed, talon will get full schema-aware validation automatically — no talon code change needed.

Reproduce: talon gateway call config.schema | grep -E '"$ref":' | head; jq 'keys[] | select(. == "$defs")' returns nothing.

title: Secrets: macOS Keychain backend, no plaintext in files/env by default
description:
Policy: talon must not store secret values in ~/.talon/openclaw.json or environment variables by default. Replacements should reference a keychain-backed provider.

Current state:
- ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json holds plaintext secrets (gateway.auth.token, channels.telegram.botToken, plugins.entries.brave.config.webSearch.apiKey, skills.entries.openai-whisper-api.apiKey).
- The existing ~/.openclaw/bin/openclaw-gateway-with-1password shim already uses 'security find-generic-password' to fetch a 1Password service-account token from the macOS Keychain, then exports it as OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN. So Keychain is already on the bootstrap path for 1P users.

Scope:
1. Define a talon-side SecretStore interface (Get/Set/Delete by service+account+key).
2. Implement a macOS Keychain backend (Go: prefer github.com/zalando/go-keyring for cross-platform abstraction, fall back to /usr/bin/security CLI shell-out if cgo is undesirable). Linux (libsecret) and Windows (Credential Manager) are bonus targets.
3. Decide the on-disk shape: when 'talon config set' targets a known-secret path, write a SecretRef pointer into ~/.talon/openclaw.json instead of the literal value. Shape options:
   (a) Reuse openclaw's SecretRef ({source, provider, id}) and add a 'keychain' source — requires openclaw runtime support to resolve.
   (b) Introduce a 'talon-secret://service/account' URI form — talon-only, openclaw won't resolve it.
   (c) Bridge: talon writes an 'exec'-source SecretRef pointing at a 'talon secret-resolve' subcommand that reads from Keychain. Works with openclaw today via the existing exec provider.
4. Detect known-secret paths (registry of paths considered sensitive: gateway.auth.token, gateway.auth.password, channels.*.{botToken,token}, plugins.entries.*.config.*.apiKey, skills.entries.*.apiKey, etc.).
5. CLI surface: 'talon config set --keychain' (force keychain backend), 'talon config set' on a known-secret path (default keychain), 'talon secrets list/get/set/delete' for direct management.
6. Migration helper: 'talon secrets migrate' scans ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json for plaintext secrets and offers to move them into Keychain + write talon-overlay refs.

Open questions:
- Native 1Password (op CLI shell-out, or 1P Connect HTTP API, or 1P SDK) vs extending the existing shim. Native gives non-Mac portability and avoids the bootstrap-token-in-Keychain step, but pulls in a heavier dep. Decide before implementation; may end up shipping both modes.
- Coordination with openclaw: option (a) above needs upstream changes; option (c) works today but adds an exec hop.
- Test strategy: keychain access prompts the user. Need a fake-store backend for unit tests, plus an integration-test harness that uses a sandbox keychain (security create-keychain).

Depends on talon-ekv landing first (SecretRef shape parity) so we have the data types to point at.

title: talon-gateway: SIGHUP handler that re-reads merged config (Phase 2 of talon-5zx)
description:
Phase 1 of talon-5zx shipped the path-class registry and CLI hints. Phase 2: make talon's embedded gateway server (internal/server/) actually honor SIGHUP by re-reading the layered config and applying changes for paths classified as ReloadHUP.

Scope:
1. Wire signal.Notify(SIGHUP) in cmd/talon/gateway.go's gatewayRunCmd alongside SIGINT/SIGTERM (today only the latter trigger shutdown).
2. On SIGHUP, call into a new server.Server.Reload(ctx, newCfg) that swaps in a new config snapshot. Concurrent RPC handlers must observe the new value on their next access (atomic.Pointer[Config] or sync.Mutex around a *Config field).
3. Decide what's actually reloadable: this PR only commits to the talon embedded-gateway side. internal/server today only serves 'health' so the reloadable surface is small; once more handlers land, more paths can move from ReloadNextRPC to ReloadHUP in internal/config/reload.go.
4. Cannot reload: listener address (port/bind), TLS material, plugin loader state — those stay ReloadRestart.
5. Tests: signal an in-process *server.Server with a fake SIGHUP-equivalent (exposed Reload method called directly), verify config swap, no goroutine leaks.
6. Docs: docs/architecture.md gains a 'Reload semantics' section under 'Embedded gateway'.

Also covers the upstream openclaw side: talon's CLI hints recommend SIGHUP for hup-class paths, but if openclaw's gateway doesn't handle SIGHUP, the user's signal is a no-op. File a separate openclaw issue if confirming that. For now, talon's hints are honest — 'send SIGHUP (or restart)' covers both cases.

value: Roadmap signal (2026-04-27): parallel subagents are a near-term priority. ADK is a candidate runtime for the subagent layer but not for memory alone. The user is open to alternatives. Don't fold subagent infrastructure into memory work — they're separate features.

openclaw plugin trust model (2026-04-27): existing openclaw plugins (Node JS in dist/extensions/) load via require() and have ambient OS authority — fs/net/exec — by design. No way to bolt gRPC capability gates onto them without rewriting. The compat shim subprocess hosts them; they run as the shim does, with full user permissions to OS resources. This isn't a regression vs openclaw (same ambient authority they always had). Native gRPC plugins get the tight capability-gated model; shim-hosted openclaw plugins get crash isolation + in-process state isolation but NOT OS-level isolation. Document this clearly: the trust line for openclaw plugins is 'you already trusted them when you enabled the plugin'. Tighter later via OS sandboxing of the shim subprocess (seccomp/landlock on Linux, sandbox-exec on darwin).

Plugin permissions design (2026-04-27): capability-gated gRPC is the primary isolation layer. Manifest declares what a plugin requests; host enforces. CRITICAL: allow user-grantable escalation — a user can opt to grant specific plugins/agents broader capabilities than the manifest's default ask (e.g. full filesystem access for an admin/deepwork agent). Effective capability set = manifest needs ∪ user grants − user denies. Don't bake workspace-confinement as an invariant; make it the default-on policy that's configurably overridable.

Per-agent tool scope (2026-04-27): tool confinement (currently workspace-only for read/write/bash) is the SAFE default but must be per-agent overridable. A user may legitimately want one agent (e.g. deepwork) to have full filesystem access while keeping another (e.g. research) workspace-confined. When implementing the plugin/tool capability system, design for the per-agent override case from day one — retrofit is expensive.

Performance hint (2026-04-27): user knows markdown parsing is slow on hot paths and plans to revisit (e.g. with a faster memory store like mem0/Letta). For now, use simple/correct over fast and leave clean swap-out points; don't optimize MD reads prematurely.

Project priority (2026-04-27): the user explicitly values that talon is 'so much faster than openclaw'. Speed/latency is a load-bearing differentiator — preserve it when making architectural decisions (favor persistent connections, in-process state, avoiding extra hops; be skeptical of features that add latency even when they look 'cleaner').

Provider integration (2026-04-27): Anthropic in this project goes through Claude Code's OAuth (claude-cli profile), NOT the raw Anthropic API — that makes it the harder provider, not the easier one. First concrete provider should be OpenAI (api_key in ~/.openclaw/agents/<agent>/agent/auth-profiles.json under 'openai:default'). The provider interface is load-bearing and must be designed up-front, not bolted onto a hardcoded first-cut. Order: provider abstraction → OpenAI implementation → chat.send wired through the interface.

Architecture correction (2026-04-27): talon's PRIMARY goal is being a drop-in replacement for openclaw — that's why we mirror openclaw protocols/methods. Plugin support is REQUIRED, not optional. Two plugin paths must work: (1) existing openclaw Node.js plugins in dist/extensions/ — users shouldn't have to rewrite to migrate; (2) new native-language plugins (Go, Rust, Python, etc.) — preferred mechanism is gRPC subprocess. Native-Go-only providers (current openai/deepseek packages) are an acceptable fast path but NOT the long-term architecture. Channels, tools, providers all eventually need to flow through the plugin layer.
Push policy (2026-04-27): direct push to main is OK until the project reaches a 'usable point'. No feature branches / PRs required for now. Revisit when the gateway server can stand on its own.

Roadmap (2026-04-27): after current config-polish work (talon-7vk whitespace, talon-8eb pretty output), priority is agent/chat surface (talon-dcj chat→TUI, talon-z8h thinking deltas, talon-xhg extractAssistantText, talon-c0b sessions), then tools and plugins. Order: config polish → agents/chat → tools/plugins.
